title: Bounded allowable-torsion derived theorem
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be smooth and $g:T\to S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and let $Y=X\times_ST$ with projections $h:Y\to X$ and $e:Y\to T$ be the base-change square of [sbc-def-base-change-square]. Let $\mathcal P$ be the set of primes invertible on $S$. For every $K\in D^b_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(T_{\Et})$ [sbc-def-derived-categories-with-allowable-torsion], the exchange map of [sbc-def-base-change-map], with abelian-sheaf coefficients,
$$\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}(K):f^{-1}Rg_*K\longrightarrow Rh_*e^{-1}K,$$
is an isomorphism in the ambient derived category of abelian sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. If both its source and target are bounded, they belong to $D^b_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(X_{\Et})$, and this map is an isomorphism in that full subcategory as well.

proof.text: Regard K as a bounded-below complex, and identify abelian sheaves with sheaves of modules over ULift Z via the forgetful equivalence. The geometric stalk comparison with this equivalence, using a universe-raised point, preserves positive integer annihilators. Thus allowable torsion means torsion of invertible order on S. The already proved upstream smooth-base-change theorem for a sheaf in degree zero applies to this module sheaf. The forgetful compatibility of the bounded-below derived exchange and its invariance under isomorphism give invertibility of the abelian bounded-below exchange on every allowable-torsion sheaf in degree zero.

Choose finite cohomological bounds a,b for K. Apply the already proved library theorem DerivedCategory.Plus.isIso_app_of_bounded to the exchange natural transformation and the isomorphism-closed property of allowable-torsion sheaves. Its proof is the usual finite triangulated induction on truncations, using the degree-zero case of step 1, shifts, and the two-out-of-three theorem for morphisms of distinguished triangles. The comparison of the canonical unbounded arrow with this bounded-below exchange in [lem-sbc-abelian-derived-exchange-plus-compatibility] conjugates it by direct-image comparison isomorphisms; the ambient arrow is therefore invertible. This requires bounds only on K.

For an allowable-torsion abelian sheaf F and q >= 0, [lem-sbc-qcqs-higher-images-prime-torsion] gives the same allowable torsion on the algebraically closed geometric stalks of R^q g_*F. Enlarge an arbitrary separably closed residue field to its algebraic closure. The proved comparison [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-field-extension] is an isomorphism on stalks, so annihilators descend to the original stalk. For q < 0 the right derived functor on a sheaf has zero cohomology. The right-derived comparison identifies the bounded-below and unbounded cohomology sheaves. Hence Rg_*F is bounded below with allowable-torsion cohomology.

The allowable-torsion bounded-below property is triangulated. Its inverse image under the triangulated functor Rg_* is also triangulated. Apply the already proved library DerivedCategory.prop_of_bounded to K and step 3: finite truncation induction proves allowable torsion of Rg_*K. Exact inverse image commutes with cohomology, and the shared inverse-image preservation lemma [lem-sbc-allowable-torsion-upper-star] transports allowable annihilators. Therefore the source of the exchange has allowable-torsion cohomology. Under the given boundedness hypothesis it lies in the bounded allowable-torsion subcategory. The ambient isomorphism from step 2 transfers this membership to the target; the full-subcategory inclusion reflects isomorphisms and proves the final clause.

proof_origin.place: B2 stage-3 proof: bounded triangulated devissage using the proved library PlusDevissage and Devissage theorems; no hypercohomology spectral sequence is needed. Lean implementation in Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.BoundedAllowableTorsionSmoothBaseChange. The allowable inverse-image lemma is reused from its shared module after relocation from the bounded-below caller.
